big_story.headline: India Defies Asia Tech Rout
big_story.subhead: OIL SLIDE AND FOREIGN BUYING CUSHION MARKETS AS GLOBAL STOCKS TUMBLE
paragraphs: As global markets face a severe sell-off and tech stocks tumble worldwide, Indian benchmark indices continue to hold firm. Overseas funds have pumped in ₹14,975 crore, providing robust support to domestic equities amidst widespread international volatility.

The resilience on Dalal Street comes even as Wall Street suffered a major crash, with major US indices plunging significantly. Meanwhile, falling oil prices and strong foreign institutional buying have helped insulate the local economy from the broader Asian tech rout.

Investors are closely watching macroeconomic indicators and global crude movements as the Nifty navigates overbought territory. Analysts suggest that domestic tailwinds and institutional liquidity will remain key drivers for Indian equities in the near term.
big_story.pullbox: Despite severe global headwinds and a tech rout across major international exchanges, India's markets remain resilient backed by strong foreign fund inflows.

explains.title: What is Foreign Portfolio Investment?
paragraphs: Foreign Portfolio Investment involves investors purchasing securities such as stocks and bonds residing in another country. It provides individuals and institutions with international diversification for their investment portfolios.
In practice, large institutional flows from overseas investors can significantly influence domestic market liquidity and asset prices, acting as a powerful buffer during global downturns.

Cosmoserve has successfully raised $6 million in seed funding to advance its innovative space debris removal technology. The startup aims to achieve full commercialisation of its orbital cleanup solutions by 2028.

The latest capital injection will accelerate research and development efforts as the company targets growing commercial demand for sustainable space operations. Backers are betting on the burgeoning commercial space economy and the urgent need to manage orbital congestion.

paragraphs: As the trading session unfolds, investors are weighing multiple indicators ranging from Gift Nifty trends to the broader Nikkei selloff. Market participants continue to track these global and domestic developments closely to gauge short-term direction.
The interplay of international cues and local sentiment remains a critical driver for domestic indices as the trading week progresses.

story_2.headline: Sensex holds firm despite Wall Street crash
paragraphs: Domestic indices displayed remarkable resilience as the Sensex held firm despite a severe Wall Street crash. Meanwhile, the Nifty experienced some downward pressure, slipping below the psychological threshold.
Traders are closely watching how local equities absorb the broader international selloff, contrasting sharply with severe pullbacks seen across major Western benchmarks.

geopolitics.headline: US Midterm Aftermath and the India Trade Deal
paragraphs: Following the US midterm elections, experts suggest that a setback for President Trump could pave the way to fast-track an India-US interim trade deal within two months. Analysts point out that a Democrat-controlled Congress or a political rout may prompt Washington to ease pressures, bringing relief to India on tariffs and visa regulations. While sources indicate that the core bilateral interim trade agreement remains on track regardless of the midterm results, opinions remain divided on how a complex Washington landscape will impact future negotiations.

At the same time, institutions like CareEdge warn that while the midterms may offer some trade relief, specific tariff and visa risks persist for Indian interests. Ex-diplomats and trade analysts argue that President Trump retains significant executive power on tariffs and foreign policy matters like Iran. As New Delhi navigates this evolving geopolitical shift, businesses await clearer signals on how the American political balance will shape upcoming trade pacts and investment flows.

big_story.headline: ONGC Q2 Consolidated PAT Jumps 47%
big_story.text: ONGC reported a massive jump in its Q2 consolidated PAT, soaring 47% YoY to Rs 18,535 crore, alongside an interim dividend announcement of Rs 8/share. This stellar performance by the energy behemoth signals robust domestic production and strong cash flows, bolstering broader investor confidence in India's core public sector enterprises.

venture_vault.headline: altM Raises $10.3M for Agri-Chemicals
venture_vault.text: Deep-tech startup altM secured $10.3 million in funding to scale the production of specialty chemicals derived from agricultural waste. Founded by former Tesla executives, the company transforms materials like rice straw and bagasse into high-value items, offering a sustainable dual solution for India's stubble burning crisis and industrial chemical demands.

venture_vault.headline: Bombay Coated Debuts at 12% Premium
venture_vault.text: Bombay Coated & Special Steels made a strong entry on the bourses, listing at a 12% premium over its IPO price. The successful market debut underscores sustained retail and institutional appetite for niche manufacturing and specialty steel segments within India's expanding industrial landscape.
